current_answer: As of 28 September 2026, public evidence does not establish a broad decline in popular models’ core capability. Anthropic’s new Opus 5.5 release claims selected gains and changes to speed, communication, price, and plan limits; METR’s preliminary five-task predeployment evaluation finds a likely modest improvement over Fable 5.1, not a large general jump. A popular Reddit thread and one creator’s blind test report improved feel or task-specific preferences, but do not measure whether an unchanged version declined and recovered or whether users returned. Anthropic’s 22 September availability incident was resolved; status pages were operational at the latest check. GPT-6 Sol’s negative Bug Hunt coding slice and near-tied Braintrust API result remain cross-sectional and method-specific. After a poor run, check status and replay the same task with version, surface, route, effort, tools, context, budget, cost/access, and final artifact recorded.

catalogue_card.question: Are AI models getting worse—or did the product change?
catalogue_card.text: No broad decline is proven. Opus 5.5 has positive selected-task evidence and “Claude is back” reports, but neither is a recovery test.

summary: No broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven.
Anthropic reports selected Opus 5.5 gains and lower typical task costs, faster output, clearer communication, and higher plan limits; these are provider claims about a new release.

METR’s unpaid preliminary assessment uses API access over ten business days and five selected AI-R&D tasks, and finds a likely modest gain over Fable 5.1; it does not test ordinary production or consumer workflows.
A Reddit “Claude is back” post and a creator’s blind task comparison are positive but self-selected signals, not evidence of recovery, representative demand, or repeat use.
Anthropic records a resolved 80-minute 22 September incident affecting requests to Opus 5, Fable 5/5.1, and Mythos 5/5.1; the page showed no 27–28 September incidents at check.
GPT-6 Sol evidence remains mixed by task: Bug Hunt has a negative coding slice, while Braintrust’s separate 175-example API test is nearly tied.
Check incident status, then replay the same task on the same surface with release, route, effort, tools, context, budget, cost/access, and final artifact recorded.
uncertainty: Anthropic’s benchmark and efficiency claims are provider-authored and do not estimate experience on every surface.
METR’s preliminary evaluation is limited to five AI-R&D tasks; Anthropic had an opportunity to review and edit the public summary.
Reddit and practitioner reports are not representative; no return-use, switch, or payment denominator is available.
The 22 September availability incident and positive release reports are on the same date, but no causal link is shown.
Bug Hunt has few runs and Braintrust uses another API task suite; neither is a fixed production time series.
Provider status is aggregate and cannot diagnose every account. Analytics, a user pilot, provider routing receipt, recovered-work measure, and payment evidence remain unavailable.
freshness_note: Fresh public-source research completed 28 September 2026. Opus 5.5 adds positive provider, preliminary selected-task, and user-reaction evidence after a version change. It does not establish recovery from model degradation; the broad-decline call remains unproven.
